lessons.claim: md.force.Custom's set_forces calls into Python every step, so it drops the run speed 26-fold on a small system (measured on an n=25 chain: bond+angle alone gives 61,264 steps/s → adding a force.Custom trap gives 2,339 steps/s). A harmonic trap can instead be made with **a ghost particle + bond.Harmonic(r0=0)** -- the function is exactly the same, U=½k r², and excluding the ghost from the integrator's filter makes it a fixed trap. Going onto the compiled path gives 55,551 steps/s (23.7x). It turned the chain-bend sweep from 25 days into 1.16 days (7 runs in parallel, 13.7 hours). ★ Before ruling 'too expensive to run', measure whether the cost is in the implementation or in the physics.
